To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a statistical machine translation approach can be used to build a stemmer, that it can be done with very few training resources, and that it can perform well in a task-based evaluation.

(1) unsupervised machine translation is a promising approach to the development of non-English stemmers; (2) the approach is applicable in any language where the stemmer is based on affix removal; (3) the approach requires only a small parallel corpus and a monolingual stemmer for its development, and can be improved using unannotated monolingual text.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an Arabic stemming model that can be trained from a small parallel corpus, and then used to process monolingual, un-annotated text.
the development of unsupervised learning approaches for the automatic extraction of linguistic knowledge from large amounts of text in a language-independent manner.
unsupervised learning of Arabic stemming, which is an important step toward building Arabic language tools that do not require large annotated training data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach to Arabic stemming is resource frugal, robust, and accurate.
this paper presents a new, novel, and promising approach to the problem of building a stemmer for a non-English language using only English and a parallel corpus.
the approach presented is a promising one that is applicable to any resource-poor language, and can produce a stemmer that performs as well as one built with human annotated data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a stemmer can be built from scratch using only a parallel corpus and an English stemmer, with no need for annotated text or a human linguist.
we are able to build a stemmer for Arabic using a parallel corpus, an English stemmer, and a small number of human annotated examples.
we have built a stemmer that is competitive with a state of art proprietary system and it is 100% data driven and does not require human intervention.
The main takeaway from our work is that
unsupervised learning can be applied to languages that are difficult to annotate, and that it is possible to build a stemmer using a very limited amount of parallel data.
unsupervised machine learning techniques can be used to build high-quality, task-specific language resources, even when the resources are not available in the target language.
a small parallel corpus and a non-English stemmer can provide a strong baseline for a new language, and can be used as a starting point for a domain-adaptable stemmer.
